title: Kidney ultrasound
what: The doctor looks at your kidneys and bladder with ultrasound. It is safe and uses no radiation.
why: For lower back pain, abnormal urine tests, high blood pressure, or suspected stones.
tell_doctor: If you have had kidney stones or kidney surgery
If you have only one kidney
If you have pain now, where it is and how long you have had it

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no special diet is needed. The day before, it is best to avoid foods that cause gas: beans, fizzy drinks, raw vegetables.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: If your bladder is checked too, you are usually asked to drink half a liter to 1 liter of water an hour before and not go to the toilet. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable. Your belly and lower back need to be bare.

bring: A urine test and past ultrasound reports, if you have them
steps: You lie on your back, then on your side or belly
The doctor puts gel on your side and lower back
Both kidneys are checked with the probe
You are asked to breathe in and hold your breath for a few seconds
If your bladder is checked, you are then asked to use the toilet and it is checked again
feel: The probe presses a little. It does not hurt
A full bladder can feel uncomfortable. It does not last long
after: You can go back to your day straight away
You usually get the report right away
red_flags: Severe lower back pain with fever, vomiting, or blood in the urine: do not wait for your appointment. Call emergency services

faq.q: Can kidney stones be seen on ultrasound?
faq.a: Yes, most kidney stones can be seen. Very small stones, or stones in the ureter, are sometimes seen better on a CT scan.

faq.q: Do I need to drink water before a kidney ultrasound?
faq.a: Not for the kidneys themselves. The bladder needs to be full, so you are often asked to drink water.

reminders.text: Kidney ultrasound soon. If the clinic asked for a full bladder, drink water an hour before and do not go to the toilet.
